newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says prices fell slower than in past.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says prices fell slower than in past.

text.p: The decline in prices of mobile handsets this year has been slower than the historical average, at some 10 to 15 percent depending on the kind of mobile phone, a senior Nokia official said on Monday.

"Price erosion has been somewhat slower than the historical average and (depending on technology) at 10 to 15 percent," Nokia investor relations vice president Martin Sandelin told analysts after the group released its first half report.
Nokia said it had solidified its leading market position in digital handsets, with 94 percent growth in the segment, and added about two-thirds of mobile phone sales were now digital.
Sandelin repeated an earlier forecast of a double-digit profit margin in mobile phones, after Nokia said it beat its H1 targets with the margin at 10 percent.
"We believe that achieving a double-digit margin in the handset business, that target still remains," he said.
All segments contributed to improved Q2 margins over Q1, he said, and although the dollar has risen strongly, currency effects were "normal occurrences."
Nokia reported first half pretax profit at 3.33 billion markka, up from 1.13 billion reported a year ago and just higher than the highest 3.3 billion forecast.
The 46 percent growth Nokia reported in Q2 group net sales would have been 42 percent with constant currencies: the 45 percent growth in H1 would have been 40 percent, he said.
Although growth was very strong, "capacity is not really an issue now (in NMP)," Sandelin said.
Nokia says it is the leading producer of digital mobile phones in the world. @

"Right now in Europe, over 90 percent of all new phones sold are digital, in Asia-Pacific somewhere between 75 and 80 percent of new phones sold are digital, the U.S. is still a large analog market ... (but) the U.S. market is continuing its transition to digital," he said.
"Over time of course, analog technologies will gradually disappear and be taken over entirely by digital," he added.

Despite strong growth, Nokia posted positive 4.2 billion markka operating cash flow. In the second half, Nokia would consume more cash, but the full-year performance would still be positive, Sandelin said. @
